Ugandan health authorities say they are on high alert after a Congolese national died from Ebola at a hospital in the capital, Kampala.
The man had travelled from Ituri province in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the centre of the current outbreak.
Officials say all those who came into contact with him have been quarantined, while temperature checks, hand sanitising measures and mask distribution have been stepped up at hospitals and border crossings.
Ugandan authorities insist the situation is under control, citing the country’s experience handling previous Ebola outbreaks and other infectious diseases.
Medical teams and aid organisations, including Médecins Sans Frontières, have also been deployed to border areas to help contain the spread of the virus.
The outbreak has raised concern across central Africa after the World Health Organization declared it a global health emergency.

Al Jazeera’s Catherine Soi reporting from Kampala, Uganda.

description:
The UAE has reported a drone strike near the Barakah nuclear power plant in the Al Dhafra region, with a fire breaking out in an electric generator outside the inner perimeter of the plant. No injuries were reported, and authorities say there has been no impact on the plant's safety.
Journalist Natasha Turak, joining Al Jazeera from Dubai, said no one has claimed responsibility for the attack and Iran has been silent. She noted that the strike appears "quite deliberate," given the plant's remote and isolated location. It follows a pattern of drone and missile attacks that have been overwhelmingly from Iran targeting the UAE's vital power infrastructure. Iran has launched nearly 3,000 attacks via missiles or drones at the UAE — more than any other country in the region, including Israel.

description:
Tensions over the Strait of Hormuz are intensifying as Iran asserts control over the strategic waterway, saying it is a sovereign responsibility shared with Oman and not the United States.

Tehran says the strait remains open but restricted for adversaries, and insists that all maritime movement through the key chokepoint must be coordinated with Iranian authorities. However, shipping activity remains below pre-war levels despite a slight increase in vessel traffic.

The Strait of Hormuz has become a central point of contention in ongoing negotiations aimed at ending the war, alongside disputes over Iran’s nuclear programme, sanctions relief, frozen assets and war reparations.

The United States’ naval blockade and Iran’s demands for lifting restrictions on its vessels have further complicated diplomatic efforts. Tehran is also seeking security guarantees to prevent renewed cycles of conflict.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Sudan’s army says it has regained control of Kur Hassan in Blue Nile state after fierce fighting with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

The clashes are part of a wider battle for control of one of Sudan’s most resource-rich regions. Blue Nile state contains vast agricultural land producing cotton, sesame and gum arabic, along with gold, copper and iron deposits concentrated in the south and southeast where fighting is intensifying.

The region is also home to the strategic Roseires Dam, a key hydroelectric facility on the Blue Nile. Sudan has accused Ethiopia of supporting RSF operations in the area, claims Addis Ababa denies.

Local leaders say the conflict is unlike previous wars fought in the region and warn that control over border zones and mineral resources could shape the wider course of Sudan’s civil war.

AL Jazeera's Hiba Morgan reports
